text: In my earlier book, Theophilus, I covered everything Jesus began to do and teach,
right up to the day he was taken up into heaven, after giving instructions through the Holy Spirit to the apostles he had chosen.
After his suffering he showed himself alive to them with many convincing proofs, appearing to them across forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.
Once, while sharing a meal with them, he told them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for what the Father had promised, something he said he had already told them about —
John baptized people with water, but in just a few days they would be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
So when they had all come together, they asked him, Lord, is this the time you are going to restore the kingdom to Israel?
He told them, It isn't your business to know the times or dates the Father has set by his own authority.
But you will be given power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, throughout Judea and Samaria, and all the way to the ends of the earth.
After he said this, he was lifted up while they watched, and a cloud took him out of their view.
While they were still staring into the sky as he went, two men dressed in white suddenly stood next to them
and said, Men of Galilee, why are you standing here staring at the sky? This same Jesus, taken from you up into heaven, will return in the very same way you watched him leave.
Then they made their way back to Jerusalem from the hill known as the Mount of Olives, a walk of about a Sabbath day's distance from the city.

Once inside, they climbed to the upstairs room where they were lodging — Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
All of them stayed devoted together in prayer, joined by some of the women, by Mary the mother of Jesus, and by his brothers.
During those days Peter got up among the gathered believers, roughly a hundred and twenty of them, and said,
Brothers, the Scripture the Holy Spirit spoke long ago through David about Judas, who led the men who seized Jesus, had to come true.
He had been counted as one of our number and shared in this same work.
(With the payment for his crime, Judas purchased a plot of land, and there he fell forward, his body split open, and everything inside him spilled out.
Word of this reached everyone living in Jerusalem, so they gave that field a name in their own tongue, Akeldama, which means Field of Blood.)
For it stands written in the Psalms: Let his dwelling become deserted, let no one live there, and, let another take up his position.
So it's necessary to choose someone who was with us the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among us,
starting from John's baptism until the day Jesus was taken up from us — this person must join us as a witness to his resurrection.
So they put forward two candidates: Joseph, known as Barsabbas and also called Justus, and Matthias.
Then they prayed, Lord, you know what is in every heart. Show us which of these two you have chosen
to take up this position of service and apostleship that Judas gave up to go where he belonged.
Then they cast lots, and the lot fell on Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles.
